pages.title: Read the situation
pages.instruction: Read the account and identify what happened and what is still unknown
pages.subject: The organiser’s proposal
paragraphs: The organiser proposes four evening sessions each month, with at least 48 hours’ notice. The aim is to keep regular contact and leave fewer questions unresolved between meetings.
Written updates and fewer live meetings are open for discussion. The organiser has not said that every question requires a meeting.

pages.title: Read the situation
pages.instruction: Read the account and identify what happened and what is still unknown
pages.subject: The participant’s constraints
paragraphs: The participant supports regular contact but can attend only two evenings a month. They need at least seven days’ notice to arrange their other responsibilities.
They are willing to send short written updates between meetings. The obstacle is the proposed frequency and notice period, rather than opposition to keeping in touch.

pages.title: Practise the conversation
pages.instruction: You are Ana and Teacher is Kim. Practise together, swap roles, then answer the questions

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: How do you feel about moving our group sessions to four evenings a month?
lines.audioText: How do you feel about moving our group sessions to four evenings a month?
lines.translation: O que acha de passar nossos encontros do grupo para quatro noites por mês?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: I can see the value of more regular contact. Even so, four evenings would be difficult for me
lines.audioText: I can see the value of more regular contact. Even so, four evenings would be difficult for me.
lines.translation: Vejo o valor de um contato mais regular. Mesmo assim, quatro noites seriam difíceis para mim

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Is the number of sessions the main problem, or the notice?
lines.audioText: Is the number of sessions the main problem, or the notice?
lines.translation: O principal problema é a quantidade de encontros ou a antecedência?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Both. I can commit to two, and I need seven days’ notice to arrange things
lines.audioText: Both. I can commit to two, and I need seven days’ notice to arrange things.
lines.translation: Ambos. Posso me comprometer com dois e preciso de sete dias de antecedência para me organizar

pages.title: Practise the conversation
pages.instruction: You are Ana and Teacher is Kim. Practise together, swap roles, then answer the questions

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: The proposal only gives forty-eight hours. Could you accept that occasionally?

lines.text: Much as I’d like to be flexible, I can’t promise attendance at that notice

lines.translation: Por mais que queira ser flexível, não posso prometer presença com essa antecedência

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: What alternative would still give the group useful contact?
lines.audioText: What alternative would still give the group useful contact?
lines.translation: Que alternativa ainda daria um contato útil ao grupo?

lines.speaker: Ana

questions.prompt: Why can’t Ana accept the original notice period?
questions.answer: Forty-eight hours doesn’t give Ana enough time to arrange attendance

pages.title: Practise the conversation
pages.instruction: You are Ana and Teacher is Kim. Practise together, swap roles, then answer the questions

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Would you agree to a four-week trial before reviewing it?
lines.audioText: Would you agree to a four-week trial before reviewing it?
lines.translation: Concordaria com um teste de quatro semanas antes de avaliar?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Yes, provided the dates are agreed a week ahead. The trial shouldn’t erase that limit
lines.audioText: Yes, provided the dates are agreed a week ahead. The trial shouldn’t erase that limit.
lines.translation: Sim, desde que as datas sejam combinadas uma semana antes. O teste não deveria apagar esse limite

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Then the shared interest is regular contact; frequency and notice are the variables
lines.audioText: Then the shared interest is regular contact; frequency and notice are the variables.
lines.translation: Então o interesse comum é contato regular; frequência e antecedência são as variáveis

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Exactly. We can make a concession without implying that every condition is negotiable
lines.audioText: Exactly. We can make a concession without implying that every condition is negotiable.
lines.translation: Exatamente. Podemos ceder em um ponto sem sugerir que toda condição é negociável

pages.title: Negotiate what you can accept

pages.title: Build concessive clauses
pages.instruction: Acknowledge one point while showing that a limit still applies

rows.subject: Neutral concession
rows.example: Although I value the sessions, I need more notice

rows.subject: A stronger degree of concession
rows.verb: Much as + subject + verb, main clause
rows.example: Much as I’d like to attend, I can offer only two evenings

rows.subject: Regardless of degree
rows.verb: However + adjective / adverb + subject + verb, main clause
rows.example: However useful the sessions are, I still need seven days’ notice

pages.note: However useful … means no matter how useful … . It is different from the sentence connector However, … . Keep the complete clause after although and much as.

pages.title: Read and explain the evidence
pages.instruction: Answer the questions using the text. Point to the detail that supports each answer

pages.title: Listen and answer
pages.instruction: Frequency changes, notice does not. Listen for the new information and decide how to respond
pages.message: Hi, Ana. I’ve thought about the group-session proposal. I can accept two live sessions a month instead of four, and I’m happy to try short written updates between them. I still need the dates confirmed at least seven days ahead; reducing the frequency doesn’t remove that planning need. Could we treat the two-session arrangement as a four-week trial and review whether the updates cover the gaps? We seem to agree on regular contact and a trial. The sticking point is not willingness to participate, but the notice required to make participation feasible. Please could you confirm that part explicitly before we tell the group the whole proposal has been accepted?
pages.audioText: Hi, Ana. I’ve thought about the group-session proposal. I can accept two live sessions a month instead of four, and I’m happy to try short written updates between them. s_mission.title: Frequency and notice

questions.prompt: How do the proposed frequency and the participant’s availability differ?
questions.answer: The organiser proposes four evenings a month, but the participant can attend only two.
questions.hint: Compare the two monthly totals in paragraph one.

questions.prompt: Why does the participant need seven days’ notice?
questions.answer: They need time to arrange their other responsibilities.
questions.hint: Find the reason immediately after the notice period.

questions.prompt: What form of contact is the participant willing to use between meetings?
questions.answer: They are willing to use short written updates.
questions.hint: Find the alternative to live sessions.

referenceParagraphs: The organiser proposes four evening sessions per month with 48 hours’ notice, aiming for useful, regular contact. The participant supports that aim but can attend only two evenings a month.
The participant needs at least seven days’ notice to arrange other responsibilities. They are willing to use short written updates between live sessions.

s_reply.title: The four-week trial

questions.prompt: Which two forms of contact have they agreed to use?
questions.answer: They have agreed to use live sessions and short written updates.
questions.hint: Find both parts of the agreement in the first sentence.

questions.prompt: How much notice is still required for session dates?
questions.answer: At least seven days’ notice is still required.
questions.hint: Look for the requirement that remains unchanged.

questions.prompt: When will they review the arrangement, and what will they assess?
questions.answer: After four weeks, they will assess whether it provides useful, regular contact.
questions.hint: Find both the trial length and the review criterion.

referenceParagraphs: The organiser and participant have agreed on two live sessions per month, with short written updates between them. Session dates must still be supplied at least seven days in advance.
They will try the arrangement for four weeks, then review whether it provides useful, regular contact. The trial changes the frequency of live meetings, not the participant’s notice requirement.
